analysis.title: Last Call At The Bank Of Nvidia: New CEO To Shut "Open Checkbook" As Huang's Final Warning To Neoclouds Emerges
key_insights: WSJ reports interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to rein in Nvidia's dealmaking after a period in which Nvidia financed compute deals and startup investments. Jensen Huang had begun the pullback months before he resigned.

Huang told neocloud executives at the October Berlin event that Nvidia's days as an open checkbook were over. Companies wanting GPU allocations would need upfront payments from their own customers, which would ease project financing and end Nvidia's role as sole financial backer.

Over the past year Nvidia provided backstops to emerging companies, lent its balance sheet to data center debt financings, and rented chips back from some customers so lenders would see contracted revenue. The financing program was announced in July, and by August Huang and Kress were questioning the returns.

Nvidia's off-balance-sheet commitments and guarantees reached $530B at end of July per the 10-Q, led by $279B of supply and capacity purchases, which rose from $119B three months earlier. Funding buyers while owing suppliers is the mismatch Kress now faces.

The $500B chip-financing platform unveiled in August with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman and KKR has produced no deal yet per Bloomberg. Lenders are pushing Nvidia to backstop more than the 25% it offered. Reuters says the platform is unlikely to disappear but riskier bets are harder to fund.

Competitors are offering similar incentives. Broadcom is backstopping roughly 72.5% of a $63B deal for Anthropic's TPUs, nearly three times Nvidia's coverage. Tightening financing risks ceding share to Google, AMD and Broadcom.
UBS's Tim Arcuri warned that even a temporary pause in Nvidia dealmaking could pull $50B or more out of the AI ecosystem while rates are rising.

Nvidia took part in a record 129 venture deals in 2026 through Nov 10, versus 49 in all of 2023. Those deals account for 27% of global VC deal value per PitchBook. Perplexity closed a $3B Nvidia investment on Oct 30, while Reflection AI ($25B valuation) and Thinking Machines Lab ($40B valuation) deals are unfinished.

Goldman's Lee Coppersmith says client sentiment on AI is about as negative as the desk has seen in a long time. Tech was the most net sold sector on Goldman's prime book, US Info Tech long/short ratio is the lowest since 2016, and selling shifted from long liquidation to new shorts. Cash desk saw persistent Nvidia supply from long-only funds rotating into hyperscalers.
Coppersmith names financing as the bigger worry than data center construction. Goldman's chart shows AI-related investment grade spreads near 140bps versus below 100bps for non-AI issuers.

Goldman's AI Semis basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings versus nearly 16x for the S&P, while consensus expects 31% earnings growth. At the market multiple, current prices imply earnings falling about 6%. Coppersmith would buy weakness and stay disciplined on hedges.

Goldman's leveraged finance desk said neocloud earnings had helped AI debt recover last week. CoreWeave's four HY notes gained an average of 4 points, and Goldman's HY AI data center basket tightened 60bps versus 20bps for the index. This preceded the WSJ report.
Premarket Nov 17: CoreWeave -5.4%, Nebius -5.5%, IREN, Applied Digital and Core Scientific about -5% each, Nvidia -2.2% after its longest weekly losing streak since October 2012.

Nebius said customer prepayments covered over 100% of Q3 capex and expects advance payments and asset-backed financing to fund 75-85% of its planned $40-45B spend next year. The author treats this as the viable template for neoclouds.

Near-term tests: Nscale's amended IPO filing has Nvidia taking a further $1B of notes or shares around Nov 17, Nscale is negotiating financing for a $45B Anthropic data center, and Firmus is raising $3B privately including customer prepayments from Nvidia. Nvidia reports Q3 on Nov 18.

Author's view: signed commitments get honored and handshake-stage deals get repriced or die, hitting low-revenue, high-debt companies first. The author expects the stress to show in neocloud bonds and private marks before Nvidia's own results.

market_movers.rationale: Pullback in financing and a CEO transition, with $279B of supply purchase commitments still outstanding. Shares were down 2.2% premarket after the longest weekly losing streak since October 2012.
Down 5.4% premarket as belief in Nvidia support for neoclouds fades. Nvidia had agreed to buy CoreWeave's unsold cloud capacity.
Down 5.5% premarket, though its prepayment-funded model is described as the template that survives Nvidia's change.
Backstopping roughly 72.5% of a $63B Anthropic TPU deal, which may take share if Nvidia retreats from financing.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman's basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings versus nearly 16x for the S&P, with consensus growth of 31%. Goldman would buy weakness but keep hedges.
The author expects bonds and private marks to reprice first as Nvidia support recedes. Names with customer prepayments are better placed.

earnings_insights: Nvidia reports Q3 on Nov 18 (per the article, 'tomorrow'). Interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to be asked about the $500B financing platform.

Nebius said customer prepayments covered more than 100% of Q3 capex (company-reported, last week's earnings) and expects advance payments and asset-backed financing to fund 75-85% of its $40-45B planned spend next year.

trade_ideas.description: Goldman (Coppersmith): buy weakness in parts of AI rather than chase rallies, while staying disciplined on hedges
trade_ideas.rationale: AI Semis basket at 11x 2028 earnings versus nearly 16x for the S&P, and prices imply earnings falling about 6% against consensus growth of 31%.
trade_ideas.risk: AI spending growth peaking and financing getting more expensive.

risk_factors: Pullback in Nvidia financing could remove $50B or more from the AI ecosystem (UBS's Arcuri estimate).
$279B of Nvidia supply and capacity purchase commitments remain while customer funding is withdrawn.
AI-related investment grade spreads near 140bps, with borrowing costs rising as rates rise.
Neoclouds and AI startups with little revenue and high cash burn may be unable to raise capital without Nvidia.
CEO succession uncertainty: Huang's possible return, Bessent's 10-day ultimatum to the board, and the interim status of Kress.
Nvidia may lose share to Broadcom, Google and AMD if it tightens financing.
charts_described: Goldman chart from the 2027 Global Markets Outlook shows investment grade spreads for AI-related issuers at roughly 140bps, near the Liberation Day peak for the rest of the market, while non-AI spreads sit below 100bps.
PitchBook chart of Nvidia venture deals rising from 11 in 2016 and 49 in 2023 to 129 in 2026 with seven weeks left in the year.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman prime book: tech was the most net sold sector last week, the US Info Tech long/short ratio is the lowest since 2016, and selling moved from long liquidation to new shorts.
Goldman cash desk saw persistent Nvidia supply from long-only funds, with money rotating into hyperscalers.
Nvidia CDS was little changed over the two weeks before the WSJ report.
geopolitical: WSJ via Reuters: the Trump administration plans to designate more than two dozen AI companies, including Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic, as national champions to help them expand overseas and compete with China.
News broke Oct 29 that Huang was seen as the target of a Chinese spy plot.
FT reports Huang has discussed a comeback, and Treasury Secretary Bessent gave the board 10 days and wants an outside CEO.
cross_bank_references: UBS's Tim Arcuri warned a temporary pause in Nvidia dealmaking could pull $50B or more out of the AI ecosystem.
Goldman's James Schneider: existing commitments should hold but new deals of the same size may be harder to put together.
Goldman's TMT specialist sales desk: the key uncertainty is whether a new CEO will have the same willingness or authority to deploy the balance sheet aggressively.
JPMorgan's TMT desk: does not expect hyperscalers to change near-term infrastructure plans solely because Huang departed, but adds uncertainty.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman's Coppersmith says signed commitments should hold, the AI Semis basket at 11x 2028 earnings already implies earnings falling about 6% against 31% consensus growth, and positioning is washed out. He would buy weakness.
tension_points.bear_case: Huang told neoclouds to secure customer prepayments, Kress is expected to pull back further, AI IG spreads are near 140bps, and startups with little revenue may be unable to raise capital. The author expects repricing in neocloud bonds and private marks.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Nvidia's Q3 report on Nov 18 and Kress's commentary on the $500B financing platform. The article also flags the Nscale $1B investment and the Anthropic West Virginia data center financing as near-term tests.

theme_stances.key_argument: A lender of last resort that starts asking for collateral has stopped being one, and weaker neocloud and startup credits get repriced first.
theme_stances.evidence: A lender of last resort that starts asking for collateral has stopped being one
